What teens practice

Stay calm. Get safe. Make choices. Be a good partner.

Balance

Stay steady and centered as a partner moves with resistance.

Escape

Get out of uncomfortable and disadvantaged positions safely.

Control

Hold positions and manage leverage without hurting a partner.

Adapt

Change your plan under pressure when the situation changes.

Cross-training

Already play a sport?

Keep playing it.

Jiu-jitsu develops athletic literacy that transfers everywhere:

  • Balance and body awareness
  • Grip strength and hand fighting
  • Core stability and scrambling
  • Cardiovascular conditioning
  • Composure against live physical resistance

What happens in class

Coached partner practice & adult on-ramp

Teens learn positions, test solutions against resistance, and review with Coach Sandy. As maturity and skill progress, teens gain access to advanced technical study and adult rounds.

See How Class Works

Questions parents & teens ask

Before the first class

Does a teen need prior experience?

No. Every student starts with fundamental movement, safe falling, and matched partner pacing.

Is this striking or fighting?

No punches or kicks. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu is 100% submission grappling, leverage, and positional control.

Can parents watch?

Yes. The studio is open and parents are welcome to observe.

Start with a calm, coached first visit.
